summary: Cyproheptadine is a sedating first-generation antihistamine with additional antiserotonergic and anticholinergic properties. It is used for allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, urticaria/angioedema, cold urticaria, dermatographism, and as adjunctive therapy in anaphylaxis after acute measures. Its antiserotonergic action also underlies off-label uses such as appetite stimulation and serotonin syndrome management. It is contraindicated in newborns, nursing mothers, and angle-closure glaucoma.

Mild uncomplicated allergic skin manifestations: urticaria and angioedema
Amelioration of allergic reactions to blood or plasma
Adjunctive therapy in anaphylaxis after acute manifestations are controlled

moa: Cyproheptadine competitively antagonizes histamine at H1 receptors, relieving allergic symptoms, and antagonizes serotonin at 5-HT2 receptors, which contributes to appetite stimulation and its use in serotonin-mediated conditions. It also has anticholinergic activity, accounting for drying and sedative effects.

missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is near the next dose, skip it and do not double up.
overdose: Overdose causes prominent anticholinergic and CNS effects: hallucinations, excitation (especially in children), CNS depression, fixed dilated pupils, flushing, hyperthermia, seizures, and cardiorespiratory collapse. Provide supportive care, control seizures and hyperthermia, and monitor cardiac status; there is no specific antidote, though physostigmine may be considered for severe anticholinergic toxicity.
